units.en: I humbly ask that a special edict announce to the realm that last year's measures did not come from Your Majesty's heart and that today's gracious labor now offers renewed imperial favor.
units.literal: I humbly beg a special edict be issued, announced far and near, making clear that last year's arrangements did not come from the imperial heart, and that today's anxious toil specially bestows sagely grace.

units.zh: 望以中書條件及王松等所論事節，委銓司點檢，務在酌中，以為定制。」
units.en: I ask that the Secretariat's conditions and the points raised by Wang Song and others be entrusted to the Selection Office for review, with moderation as the fixed rule."
units.literal: I hope the Secretariat conditions and the matters Wang Song and others discussed may be entrusted to the selection office for inspection, striving to strike the mean and become fixed regulations."

units.zh: 朝廷移授昭義節度使，璋謀欲不奉詔，判官邊蔚密言規責，乃僶勉承命。
units.en: When the court reassigned him to the Zhaoyi circuit, Zhang considered defying the order. Only after his secretary Bian Wei quietly reprimanded him did he grudgingly accept.
units.literal: The court transferred him to the Zhaoyi military commissionership. Zhang planned to refuse the decree, but his aide Bian Wei privately admonished him, and he reluctantly accepted.

units.zh: 明宗嗣位，錄平蜀功，授邠州節度使。
units.en: When Emperor Mingzong took the throne, Zhang's role in the conquest of Shu was formally acknowledged, and he was given Binzhou as his circuit.
units.literal: When Emperor Mingzong succeeded to the throne, Zhang's service in pacifying Shu was recognized, and he was appointed military commissioner of Binzhou.

units.zh: 丁丑，以前西京副留守梁文矩為兵部尚書。
units.en: On dingchou former western capital vice defender Liang Wenju became war minister.
units.literal: On dingchou, former western capital vice defender Liang Wenju became War Minister.

units.zh: 壬午，以前秦州節度使李德充為定州節度使兼北面行營副招討使。
units.en: On renwu former Qin commissioner Li Dechong became Ding commissioner and deputy northern campaign suppression commissioner.
units.literal: On renwu, former Qinzhou military commissioner Li Dechong was made Dingzhou military commissioner and deputy northern campaign suppression commissioner.

units.zh: 樞密院學士、尚書倉部郎中司徒詡，樞密院學士、尚書工部郎中顏衎並落職守本官，樞密副使張從恩改宣徽使：初廢樞密院故也。
units.en: Situ Xu and Yan Kan, academicians of the Bureau of Military Affairs, were stripped of their concurrent posts and retained their original offices; Zhang Cong'en, vice commissioner of the bureau, was reassigned as commissioner of the Palace Directorate—because the Bureau of Military Affairs had just been abolished.
units.literal: Situ Xu, Academician of the Bureau of Military Affairs and Director of the Granary Section of the Ministry of Revenue, and Yan Kan, Academician of the Bureau of Military Affairs and Director of the Works Section of the Ministry of Works, were both removed from their posts and retained their original offices; Zhang Cong'en, Vice Commissioner of the Bureau of Military Affairs, was changed to Commissioner of the Palace Directorate—because the Bureau of Military Affairs was first abolished.

units.zh: 辛未，以鄴都留守杜威為北面行營都招討使，以侍衛親軍都指揮使、鄆州節度使李守貞為兵馬都監，兗州安審琦為左右廂都指揮使，徐州符彥卿為馬軍左廂都指揮使，滑州皇甫遇為馬軍右廂都指揮使，貝州梁漢璋為馬軍都排陣使，前鄧州宋彥筠為步軍左廂都指揮使，奉國左廂都指揮使王饒為步軍右廂都指揮使，洺州團練使薛懷讓為先鋒都指揮使。
units.en: On xinwei Du Wei, military governor of Yedu, was appointed overall commander of the northern field army; Li Shouzhen, commander of the Imperial Guard and military governor of Yunzhou, became overall supervisor of troops and horses; An Shenqi of Yanzhou commanded both wings; Fu Yanqing of Xuzhou the left wing of cavalry; Huangfu Yu of Huazhou the right wing of cavalry; Liang Hanzhang of Beizhou marshal of the cavalry array; Song Yanyun, former prefect of Dengzhou, the left wing of infantry; Wang Rao of the Fengguo left wing the right wing of infantry; and Xue Huairang, regimental trainer of Mozhou, vanguard commander.
units.literal: On xinwei Du Wei, military governor of Yedu, was made overall commander of the Northern Circuit field headquarters; Li Shouzhen, commander of the Imperial Guard and military governor of Yanzhou, was made overall supervisor of troops and horses; An Shenqi of Yanzhou was made commander of both wings; Fu Yanqing of Xuzhou was made commander of the left wing of the horse army; Huangfu Yu of Huazhou was made commander of the right wing of the horse army; Liang Hanzhang of Beizhou was made marshal of the horse army array; Song Yanyun, former prefect of Dengzhou, was made commander of the left wing of the foot army; Wang Rao, commander of the left wing of the Fengguo army, was made commander of the right wing of the foot army; Xue Huairang, regimental trainer of Mozhou, was made vanguard commander.

units.zh: 是月，北面行營招討使杜威率諸將領大軍自鄴北征，師次瀛州城下，貝州節度使梁漢璋戰死。
units.en: That month Du Wei, northern field commander, marched a great army north from Ye with his generals; the force halted below Yingzhou, where Liang Hanzhang, military governor of Beizhou, was killed in battle.
units.literal: That month Du Wei, commander of the northern field headquarters, led the generals and a great army north from Ye on campaign; the army halted below Yingzhou city; Liang Hanzhang, military governor of Beizhou, died in battle.

units.zh: 杜威等以漢璋之敗，遂收軍而退。
units.en: After Hanzhang's defeat Du Wei and his commanders withdrew the army.
units.literal: Du Wei and the others, because of Hanzhang's defeat, then drew off the army and retreated.

units.zh: 庚辰，以少府監聶延祚為殿中監，以前雲州節度使楊漢章為安州節度使。
units.en: On gengchen Nie Yanzuo became palace supervisor and Yang Hanzhang of Yunzhou became An commissioner.
units.literal: On gengchen Court Artisan Supervisor Nie Yanzuo was made Palace Supervisor; former Yunzhou military commissioner Yang Hanzhang was made Anzhou military commissioner.

units.zh: 白再榮，本蕃部人也。
units.en: Bai Zairong was originally from the frontier tribes.
units.literal: Bai Zairong was originally a man of the barbarian tribes.

units.zh: 高祖以再榮為鎮州留後，為政貪虐難狀，鎮人呼為「白麻答」。
units.en: Gaozu made Zairong regent of Zhenzhou. His rule was so greedy and cruel that the people called him "White Mandale."
units.literal: Gaozu made Zairong regent of Zhenzhou; his governance was greedy and cruel beyond description, and the people of the garrison called him "White Mandale."

units.zh: 少從軍，累遷護聖左廂指揮使。
units.en: He entered the army young and eventually became commander of the left wing of the Husheng Guard.
units.literal: In youth he followed the army and was repeatedly transferred to commander of the left wing of the Husheng Guard.

units.zh: 翊日，逐出床答勒，諸軍以再榮名次在諸校之右，乃請權知留後事。
units.en: The next day they drove out Chuangdale. Because Zairong outranked the other commanders, the troops asked him to serve as acting regent.
units.literal: The next day they drove out Chuangdale; the armies, because Zairong's seniority ranked above the various commanders, then requested that he provisionally know regency affairs.

units.zh: 未幾，移授滑州節度使，箕斂誅求，民不聊生，乃征還京師。
units.en: Soon he was transferred to Huazhou as military commissioner, where his crushing exactions left the people destitute. He was then recalled to the capital.
units.literal: Before long he was transferred and appointed military commissioner of Huazhou; he scraped together and demanded exactions, the people could not sustain life, and he was then summoned back to the capital.

units.zh: 晉末，契丹入汴，明年，契丹主北去，再榮從部帳至真定。
units.en: Late in Jin the Khitan entered Bian. The next year, as the Khitan emperor withdrew north, Zairong followed the camp to Zhending.
units.literal: At the end of Jin the Khitan entered Bian; the next year the Khitan ruler went north, and Zairong followed the tribal encampment to Zhending.

units.zh: 其年閏七月晦，李筠、何福晉相率殺北帥滿達勒，據甲仗庫，敵勢未退，筠等使人召再榮。
units.en: On the last day of the intercalary seventh month that year, Li Jun and He Fujin led the killing of the Khitan commander Mandale and seized the armory. The enemy had not yet withdrawn, and they sent for Zairong.
units.literal: That year on the last day of the intercalary seventh month, Li Jun and He Fujin together led the killing of the northern commander Mandale, seized the armory, the enemy's strength had not yet withdrawn, and Jun and the others sent men to summon Zairong.

units.zh: 周太祖入京城，軍士攻再榮之第，迫脅再榮，盡取財貨既，軍士前啟曰：「某等軍健，常趨事麾下，一旦無禮至此，今後何顏謁見？」
units.en: When Taizu of Zhou entered the capital, soldiers stormed Zairong's house and forced him to hand over everything he owned. Then one of them said, "We have always served under you, sir. After treating you so shamefully, how can we ever face you again?"
units.literal: When Zhou Taizu entered the capital, soldiers attacked Zairong's residence, coerced Zairong, and after completely taking his valuables, the soldiers stepped forward and said: "We soldiers have always hurried to serve under your command; suddenly to be discourteous to this extent—hereafter with what face shall we pay our respects?"

units.zh: 即奮刃擊之，挈其首而去，後家人以帛贖葬之。
units.en: They at once cut him down, took his head, and left. His family later ransomed the head with silk for burial.
units.literal: They then flourished blades and struck him, took his head and left; later his family used silk to ransom it for burial.

units.zh: 再榮端坐本營，遲疑久之。
units.en: Zairong sat stiffly in his own camp, hesitating for a long while.
units.literal: Zairong sat upright in his own camp, hesitating for a long time.

units.zh: 為軍吏所迫，乃行。
units.en: Pressed by his officers, he finally went.
units.literal: Pressed by the army clerks, he then went.

units.zh: 再榮貪昧無決，舉止多疑，出入騎從，露刃註矢，諸校不相統攝，互有猜貳。
units.en: Zairong was greedy, indecisive, and suspicious. He went about surrounded by armed horsemen with blades drawn and bows strung. The commanders would not submit to one another and eyed each other with distrust.
units.literal: Zairong was greedy and dull without decision; his conduct was full of suspicion; going out and in he had mounted followers with bared blades and strung arrows; the various commanders did not command one another and mutually harbored doubt and division.

units.zh: 奉國廂主王饒懼為再榮所並，乃據東門樓，以兵自衛，偽稱足疾，不敢見再榮。
units.en: Wang Rao, commander of the Fengguo wing, feared that Zairong would swallow his command. He seized the east gate tower, garrisoned it with troops, feigned a foot ailment, and refused to see Zairong.
units.literal: Fengguo wing commander Wang Rao feared being absorbed by Zairong; he then held the east gate tower, used troops to protect himself, falsely claimed foot ailment, and did not dare see Zairong.

units.zh: 司天監趙延乂俱與之善，乃來往解釋，遂無相忌之意。
units.en: Zhao Yanyi of the Directorate of Astronomy was friendly with both men and shuttled between them until their mutual suspicion eased.
units.literal: Director of the Astronomy Bureau Zhao Yanyi was on good terms with both; he then went back and forth explaining, and thus there was no mutual suspicion.

units.zh: 再榮以李崧、和凝攜家在彼，令軍士數百人環迫崧、凝，以求賞給，崧、凝各出家財與之。
units.en: Because Li Song and He Ning had their families with them in the city, Zairong sent hundreds of soldiers to surround them and demand payment. Both men paid out of their private fortunes.
units.literal: Zairong, because Li Song and He Ning had brought their families there, ordered several hundred soldiers to surround and press Song and Ning to seek reward payments; Song and Ning each gave family wealth to them.

units.zh: 再榮欲害崧以利其財，前磁州刺史李穀謂再榮曰：「公與諸將為契丹所擄，淩辱萬端，旦夕憂死。
units.en: Zairong then planned to kill Song for his wealth. Li Gu, former prefect of Cizhou, said to him, "You and the other generals were captured by the Khitan, humiliated in every way, and lived in daily fear of death.
units.literal: Zairong wished to kill Song to profit from his wealth; former Cizhou prefect Li Gu said to Zairong: "You and the generals were captured by the Khitan, insulted in ten thousand ways, and feared death morning and evening.

units.zh: 今日眾力逐出蕃戎，鎮民死者不下三千人，豈獨公等之功！
units.en: Today the combined effort of many men drove out the barbarians, and no fewer than three thousand townspeople died. Was that victory yours alone!
units.literal: Today the multitude's strength drove out the barbarian forces; townspeople who died were not fewer than three thousand—how is it the achievement of you alone!

units.zh: 才得生路，便擬殺一宰相，他日到闕，儻有所問，何以為辭？」
units.en: You have only just won your lives, and already you would kill a chief minister. When you reach the capital, what answer will you give if you are questioned?"
units.literal: Just having gained a path to life, you now plan to kill a chief minister; when you reach the capital another day, if there should be questions, with what will you make your plea?"

units.zh: 再榮又欲括率在城居民家財，以給軍士，李穀又譬解之，乃止。
units.en: Zairong next wanted to seize the property of everyone in the city to pay the troops, but Li Gu dissuaded him again and he desisted.
units.literal: Zairong again wished to assess and seize the household wealth of residents in the city to supply the soldiers; Li Gu again explained and dissuaded him, and he then stopped.

units.zh: 其漢人曾事滿達勒者盡拘之，以取其財。
units.en: He detained every Han who had once served Mandale and stripped them of their property.
units.literal: All Han people who had once served Mandale were detained to take their wealth.

units.zh: 再榮默然。
units.en: Zairong said nothing.
units.literal: Zairong was silent.

units.zh: 以右散騎常侍張煦、給事中王延藹並為左散騎常侍，以前大名府少尹李瓊為將作監，以前彰武軍節度使周密為太子太師致仕，以衛尉卿劉皞充漢隱帝山陵部署。
units.en: Zhang Xu, Regular Attendant of the Right Cavalry, and Wang Yan'ai, Drafting Official, were both appointed Regular Attendants of the Left Cavalry; former Junior Prefect of Daming Li Qiong became Director of Palace Construction; former Military Commissioner of the Zhangwu Army Zhou Mi received retirement as Grand Tutor of the Crown Prince; and Liu Hao, Chamberlain for the Guards, was placed in charge of arrangements for Hidden Emperor of Han's mausoleum.
units.literal: Zhang Xu, Regular Attendant of the Right Cavalry, and Wang Yan'ai, Drafting Official in the Secretariat, were both made Regular Attendants of the Left Cavalry; the former Junior Prefect of Daming Fu Li Qiong was made Director of Palace Construction; the former Military Commissioner of the Zhangwu Army Zhou Mi was made retired Grand Tutor of the Crown Prince; Liu Hao, Chamberlain for the Guards, was appointed to the arrangements for the mausoleum of Emperor Yin of Han.

units.zh: 以中書舍人盧詹為禮部侍郎，以兵部侍郎裴皞為太子賓客。
units.en: Lu Zhan became vice minister of rites; Pei Hao of War became crown prince mentor.
units.literal: Secretariat drafting officer Lu Zhan was made Vice Minister of Rites; Vice Minister of War Pei Hao was made crown prince mentor.

units.zh: 子溫叟，仕至御史中丞。
units.en: His son Wensou rose to censor-in-chief.
units.literal: His son Wensou served up to Censor-in-Chief.

units.zh: 〈（《國老談苑》云：劉溫叟方正守道，以名教為己任。
units.en: (The Statesmen's Garden of Talk records that Liu Wensou was upright and principled, holding himself to the standards of proper conduct.
units.literal: (Statesmen's Garden of Talk says: Liu Wensou was upright and upheld the Way, taking name and teaching as his personal charge.

units.zh: 初為翰林學士，私庭拜母，母即命二婢箱擎公服、金帶，置於階下，謂溫叟曰：「此汝父長興中入翰林時所賜也。
units.en: When he first became a Hanlin academician, he bowed to his mother in their private courtyard. She at once had two maidservants bring out chests holding official robes and a gold belt and set them on the steps, saying, "These were granted when your father entered the Hanlin in the Changxing era.
units.literal: When he first became Hanlin academician, in the private courtyard he bowed to his mother; his mother immediately ordered two maidservants to carry in chests the official robes and gold belt, and set them on the steps below, saying to Wensou: "These were bestowed when your father entered the Hanlin in the Changxing era.

units.zh: 幼孤，事母以孝聞，其母甚賢。
units.en: Orphaned in childhood, he was famed for filial devotion to his mother, who was a woman of exceptional virtue.
units.literal: Orphaned young, he was known for filial service to his mother; his mother was very worthy.

units.zh: 自先君子薨背以來，嘗懼家門替墜，今汝能自致青雲，繼父之職，可服之無愧矣！」
units.en: Since your father's death I have feared our house would fall into decline. Now you have risen on your own merits to succeed to his post — wear them without shame!"
units.literal: Since your late father's passing I have feared the family's decline; now you can reach the blue clouds on your own, succeeding to your father's office — you may wear them without shame!"

units.zh: 溫叟伏地號慟，退就別寢，素衣蔬食，追慕數日，然後服之，士大夫以為得禮。）〉
units.en: Wensou prostrated himself and wailed aloud, then withdrew to another room, dressed in plain clothes and ate simple fare, and mourned his father for several days before putting on the robes. Men of cultivation held this to be proper ritual.)〉
units.literal: Wensou prostrated himself and wailed loudly; he withdrew to a separate chamber, wore plain clothes and ate simple food, mourned in remembrance for several days, and only then donned the robes — the gentry considered this proper ritual.)〉

units.zh: 九月辛未，以右羽林統軍周密為鄜州節度使。
units.en: In the ninth month, Zhou Mi, commander of the Right Forest Guard Army, was appointed military governor of Fu Prefecture.
units.literal: In the ninth month, on the xinwei day, Zhou Mi, Commander of the Right Forest Guard Army, was appointed Military Governor of Fu Prefecture.

units.zh: 辛亥，以太子少傅楊凝式為太子少師，以太常卿張昭為戶部尚書，以尚書左丞王易為禮部尚書，以兵部侍郎邊蔚為太常卿，以翰林學士、中書舍人魚崇諒為工部侍郎充職，以戶部侍郎韋勛為兵部侍郎，以刑部侍郎邊歸讜為戶部侍郎，以禮部侍郎司徒詡為刑部侍郎，以秘書監趙上交為禮部侍郎，以兵部尚書王仁裕為太子少保，以翰林學士、禮部尚書張沆為刑部尚書充職，以尚書右丞田敏為左丞，以吏部侍郎段希堯為工部尚書，以太子詹事馬裔孫為太子賓客。
units.en: On xinhai day, Yang Ningshi moved from Junior Tutor to Junior Preceptor of the Crown Prince; Zhang Zhao from Director of Imperial Sacrifices to Minister of Revenue; Wang Yi from Left Vice Director of State Affairs to Minister of Rites; Bian Wei from Vice Minister of War to Director of Imperial Sacrifices; Yu Chongliang, Hanlin Academician and Secretariat Drafting Official, to Vice Minister of Works; Wei Xun from Vice Minister of Revenue to Vice Minister of War; Bian Guichan from Vice Minister of Justice to Vice Minister of Revenue; Situ Xu from Vice Minister of Rites to Vice Minister of Justice; Zhao Shangjiao from Director of the Palace Library to Vice Minister of Rites; Wang Renyu from Minister of War to Junior Guardian of the Crown Prince; Zhang Hong, Hanlin Academician and Minister of Rites, to Minister of Justice; Tian Min from Right to Left Vice Director of State Affairs; Duan Xiyao from Vice Minister of Personnel to Minister of Works; and Ma Yisun from Chamberlain for the Heir Apparent to Advisor to the Crown Prince.
units.literal: On the day xinhai, Yang Ningshi, Junior Tutor of the Crown Prince, was made Junior Preceptor of the Crown Prince; Zhang Zhao, Director of the Court of Imperial Sacrifices, was made Minister of Revenue; Wang Yi, Left Vice Director of the Department of State Affairs, was made Minister of Rites; Bian Wei, Vice Minister of War, was made Director of the Court of Imperial Sacrifices; Yu Chongliang, Hanlin Academician and Secretariat Drafting Official, was made Vice Minister of Works in his office; Wei Xun, Vice Minister of Revenue, was made Vice Minister of War; Bian Guichan, Vice Minister of Justice, was made Vice Minister of Revenue; Situ Xu, Vice Minister of Rites, was made Vice Minister of Justice; Zhao Shangjiao, Director of the Palace Library, was made Vice Minister of Rites; Wang Renyu, Minister of War, was made Junior Guardian of the Crown Prince; Zhang Hong, Hanlin Academician and Minister of Rites, was made Minister of Justice in his office; Tian Min, Right Vice Director of the Department of State Affairs, was made Left Vice Director; Duan Xiyao, Vice Minister of Personnel, was made Minister of Works; Ma Yisun, Chamberlain for the Heir Apparent, was made Advisor to the Crown Prince.
